To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two examined bone graft fillers, beta tricalcum phosphate and bovine bone mineral, promote new bone formation in the augmentation sites, but the amount of new formed bone is significantly greater in bovine bone mineral sites.

bovine bone mineral (BBMin) and beta tricalciun phosphate (beta TCP), both used as bone fillers in sinus floor augmentation procedures, promote new bone formation, but the amount of new formed bone is significantly greater in BBMin grafted sites than in beta TCP grafted sites at 12 months post-augmentation.

(1) bone area fraction increased significantly with tissue depth at both grafted sides in all cores; and (2) the area fraction of newly formed bone and the residual amount of grafted material were significantly higher at the BBM than at the beta TCP grafted sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the amount of newly-formed bone and the amount of residual graft material at different depths in the augmented sinus cavity.
the effect of the residual grafted material amount and tissue depth on bone formation.
the amount of newly-formed bone in sinus floor augmentation procedures and the effect of the type and residual amounts of the grafted materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BBM is a better bone substitute in sinus grafting.
BBM is superior to beta TCP for bone formation at 12 months after sinus augmentation.
the amount of newly bone formed in sinus grafting depends on tissue depth and residual filler particles, but the osteoconductivity of the fillers also plays a role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BBM is superior to beta TCP in promoting bone formation in sinus floor augmentation.
the osteoconduction of BBM is superior to that of beta TCP.
the osteoconduction ability of bone graft substitutes is not only related to the filler material but also to the residual amount of the grafting material at the time of healing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the osteoconduction ability of the bone filler is the main factor in the newly formed bone area fraction in sinus grafting.
the amount of newly bone in sinus augmentation procedures is affected not only by tissue depth but also by the type and residual quantity of the grafted bone filler.
the osteoconducitiviy of the grafted filler is the main factor in the amount of newly-formed bone.
